newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Wall St cheers S.African industrials to firmer end.
newsitem.headline: Wall St cheers S.African industrials to firmer end.

text.p: 1435 GMT - South African industrial shares finish slightly firmer after retracing earlier losses in active afternoon trade. Dealers say industrials cheered by positive start of Wall Street and some futures play.

Golds end weaker despite better bullion. Dealers say more action seen in golds if bullion breaks above $350 an ounce. Sentiment remains good but jittery amid lack of fresh local economic factors, dealers say.
Volumes moderate with 736 million rand of shares traded.

* Liberty Life ends 450 cents up at 129.50 rand after the company announced that its new financial year had got off to a good start with new business figures for the first quarter of 1997 more than 65 percent up on the year-ago.
* De Beers ends up 75 cents at 160.50 rand on news that a deal with Russia is imminent.
* Industrials last up 19.2 points at 8,493.9, golds down 5.3 points at 1,270.1 and the all-share was up 21.4 points at 7,214.5.
